description: Earth Data Sound transforms NASA's Earth data into meaningful audio experiences, making information about our planet easier and more interesting to understand. Our goal is to combine science, technology and creativity to make Earth science more engaging and accessible through sound.
summary:
I developed Earth Data Sounds, an interactive web application for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026’s challenge, “The Earth Information Jukebox.” The project helps users experience NASA Earth-science information through both sight and sound.
The website allows users to choose one of three NASA Earth Information Center and Scientific Visualization Studio visual experiences: Night Lights, Ocean Currents and Temperature, and Aerosols. Users can select an area on the visual map, and the application analyses that selected area’s visual properties, such as brightness, colour, movement, and density. It then creates real-time sonification using the browser’s Web Audio API.
For example, brighter areas in the Night Lights visual can create higher and louder sounds, while warmer ocean colours can create higher pitches. Users can play, pause, stop, replay, and control the volume of the generated sound. The app also provides clear sound legends, NASA source information, and limitations.
Earth Data Sounds addresses the challenge by pairing NASA EIC visual frames with dynamic, real-time generated sonifications. It makes complex Earth-science information more engaging and accessible, especially for people who learn better through sound or have low vision. The project is educational, non-commercial, and built to encourage users to explore our changing planet through a new multi-sensory experience.
details: Earth Data Sounds is an interactive web application that helps users experience NASA Earth-science information through both sight and sound. It was developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge, “The Earth Information Jukebox.” The application allows users to choose one of three NASA Earth Information Center and Scientific Visualization Studio visual experiences: Night Lights, Ocean Currents and Temperature, and Aerosols. Users can select an area directly on the visual map by clicking or dragging. The application then analyses the selected area’s visual properties, including brightness, colour, colour density, visual movement, and pixel variation. Using the browser’s Web Audio API, the app converts these visual properties into real-time sonification. For example, brighter areas in the Night Lights visual can create higher and louder sounds, while warmer ocean colours can create higher pitches. More visual movement or denser aerosol patterns can create faster rhythms and richer sound textures. The sound is generated dynamically from the visual information; it is not a prerecorded audio track or a literal recording of Earth’s atmosphere. Users can play, pause, stop, replay, and adjust the volume of the sonification. The app also provides sound legends, visual descriptions, loading and error messages, and clear information about the NASA resources used. The project uses React, HTML, CSS, JavaScript/TypeScript, and the Web Audio API. It was built with Lovable.ai, an AI-assisted web development platform, and is hosted through Lovable’s publishing platform. The project uses public NASA Earth Information Center and NASA Scientific Visualization Studio resources, including the NASA SVS Search API and SVS media assets. The main benefit of Earth Data Sounds is that it makes NASA Earth-science information more engaging and accessible. It gives users an additional way to understand visual data through sound, which can support auditory learners and people with low vision. The project is educational, non-commercial, and designed to encourage curiosity about Earth’s changing systems. The team considered accessibility, simplicity, scientific accuracy, user understanding, and honest limitations. Version 1 uses a shared visual-to-sound sonification approach across the three selected NASA visual experiences. Future development could create separate sound mappings for each Earth-science feature and add more NASA EIC visual resources.
